tier_reason: The SMHasher3 results summary is a well-known independent third-party suite. It lists MeowHash at 12.43 bytes/cycle bulk against XXH-64 at 3.99, CityHash-64 at 4.75 and wyhash at 6.98, and the benchmark code is public. It is not A because neither the summary nor the raw MeowHash result names the CPU model, compiler or flags; they only give GiB/s '@ 3.5 ghz' with ncpu=1.

corrections.claimed_speedup: SMHasher3 results table: MeowHash 12.43 bytes/cycle average bulk, against XXH-64 3.99, CityHash-64 4.75 and wyhash 6.98. That is about 3.1x, 2.6x and 1.8x (derived from page data). The same table puts XXH3-64 (current xxHash) at 12.82 bytes/cycle, slightly ahead of Meow in bulk, so the win is over legacy XXH64, not XXH3.
corrections.workload: SMHasher3 bulk speed test (262144-byte and 262017-262144-byte keys, 'Alignment rnd' average), AES-NI path, single thread
corrections.hardware: Unspecified x86-64 CPU with AES-NI. SMHasher3 gives GiB/s assuming 3.5 GHz and names no CPU model.
corrections.caveats: Meow is built for large-buffer hashing. On short keys it is about 2x slower: 61.51 average cycles per hash for 1-32 bytes, against 29.31 for wyhash and 30.69 for XXH3-64. XXH3-64 (12.82 bytes/cycle) edges it out in bulk, and gxhash, falkhash and t1ha0.aesB are faster still but fail some SMHasher3 quality tests. Meow passes all 250 tests. The README security notice reclassifies v0.5 from level 3 to level 1 after Peter Schmidt-Nielsen's cryptanalysis, so it should not be used for MACs or DoS-resistant hash tables. v0.5 is still labelled a 'proposal' and never reached v1.0. mollyrocket.com/meowhash redirects to a Computer, Enhance! stub page with no benchmark data.

notes: All four numbers match the SMHasher3 summary rows exactly (MeowHash 12.43, XXH-64 3.99, CityHash-64 4.75, wyhash 6.98). The record's last_commit of 2022-07-31 was the repo's pushed_at date; the newest commit on any branch is 2021-07-02 (master). It is still abandoned, not archived, Zlib licensed, with 1,831 stars.

tier_reason: These are the author's own SMHasher3 runs on an i7-12700K, shown only as PNG charts in the README. The SMHasher3 build log shows GCC 11.3.0 under MSYS, but no flags or build type are given. The MuseAir-BFast test names suggest a local SMHasher3 variant, not the public upstream code, so this is first-party with partial methodology (C).

corrections.claimed_speedup: Not faster than wyhash overall. On 1-31 byte keys the README chart shows MuseAir and MuseAir-BFast using more cycles per hash than wyhash and rapidhash at almost every length (about 18.6 vs 15.1 cycles at 1-4 bytes, about 35-45 vs 27 at 17-31 bytes). In bulk (262144-byte keys) standard MuseAir is on par with wyhash v4.2 at about 34 GiB/s @ 3.5 GHz. The BFast line appears to be about 42 GiB/s, roughly 1.2x wyhash (read from chart; line colours repeat, so approximate). The README text claims 'up to 33.2 GiB/s' for BFast and that MuseAir 'holds its own against' wyhash, which is a parity claim.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 11.3.0 (MSYS on Windows), from the SMHasher3 cmake log in the README; flags and build type not stated
corrections.hardware: 12th Gen Intel Core i7-12700K (Windows/MSYS); GiB/s figures assume 3.5 GHz
corrections.caveats: This is a third-party C++20 port of eternal-io/museair (Rust), which is a separate catalog candidate. By the port's own charts it is slower than wyhash and rapidhash on small keys; only BFast bulk hashing looks faster. The README's 33.2 GiB/s text does not match its bulk chart (about 42 GiB/s). SMHasher3's upstream results (MuseAir.bfast 8.64 bytes/cycle bulk and 26.28 cycles for small keys, against wyhash's 6.98 and 29.31) come from SMHasher3's own CC0 MuseAir v0.3 code, not from this port. On licensing, the top badge says 'GNU' and the README License section says MIT, but the LICENSE file is GPL-3.0 (used here).

notes: I downgraded because the port's own README chart shows it slower than the wyhash baseline on 1-31 byte keys. Only BFast in bulk looks about 1.2x faster, and that reading is uncertain because the chart's line colours repeat. The tier stays C. Metadata matches the record: GPL-3.0, not a fork, 7 stars, last commit 2026-02-23 (active).
